name: Philippine Serpent-Eagle
rangeDescription: Forest of larger philippines (except palawan)
description: A fairly large, common raptor of forest and more open wooded areas from the lowlands to the lower mountains. Dark brown with white speckles on the crown and upperparts, rufous-brown below with large white spots.

name: Zino's Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds in summer in cliffs high on pico do arieiro (central madeira; central macaronesia); non-breeding range in subtropical and tropical atlantic to azores (northwestern macaronesia) and st. helena and northeastern brazil (tropical south atlantic ocean)
description: Medium-sized gadfly petrel with long, angular wings and buoyant, banking flight. Extremely similar to Cape Verde and Desertas Petrels (formerly known together as Fea’s), but slightly smaller and more compact overall with a smaller bill.

name: Pygmy Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Mountains of new guinea (bird's head peninsula to owen stanley range)
description: A tiny, green lorikeet of foothill and montane forest and edge. Uniform green plumage, light streaking on the chest and slightly elongated pointy tail.

name: Swamp Francolin
rangeDescription: Terai of northern india to southern nepal and bangladesh
description: Brown francolin with an orange throat and white-striped underparts. Shows rufous outer tail feathers and primaries in flight.

name: Gambaga Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Semiarid southern mali to ghana, kenya, somalia, and southwestern arabia
description: A drab flycatcher that is uncommon and localized across its range. Some of the key features include vague and blurry streaking on the breast and crown, short wings, and a bill that is dark above and pale below.

name: Orange-fronted Plushcrown
rangeDescription: Tropical southeastern colombia to northern bolivia and western amazonian brazil
description: Small, yellowish-tan bird. Orange face is unique, but sometimes difficult to see; a more obvious field mark is its bright orange legs.

name: LeConte's Sparrow
rangeDescription: Prairies of central north america; winters to gulf states
description: This strikingly beautiful sparrow is found in wet meadows with tall grass. Look for the bright orange-buff face with a silvery cheek, spotted purplish-gray nape, and crisp black streaking on buffy underparts.

name: Sri Lanka Gray Hornbill
rangeDescription: Moist deciduous forest of sri lanka
description: Small hornbill with gray upperside and whitish underparts. Bill has no casque, and is pale in males, dark in females.

name: Yellow-crowned Euphonia
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern nicaragua to costa rica and panama
description: Small finchlike bird, compact and short tailed. Generally yellow below and dark blue-black above with stout, short bill.

name: Anchieta's Sunbird
rangeDescription: Angola to southeastern democratic republic of the congo, zambia, southwestern tanzania, malawi, and northern mozambique
description: Small, distinctive sunbird, red and yellow below with iridescent blue on the forehead, throat, and breast. The male and female are similar, though the female is duller.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Rufous-winged Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Andes of ecuador and northwestern peru (southward to lambayeque and la libertad)
description: Small, warbler-like flycatcher found in the Andes and coastal hills. Mostly gray and white with whitish wingbars, white eyebrow, and rufous wing patches.

name: Slate-throated Gnatcatcher
rangeDescription: Tropical forest of eastern panama to northwestern ecuador
description: Uncommon from extreme eastern Panama to northwest Ecuador. Typical gnatcatcher shape: small and long-tailed.

name: Caucasian Grouse
rangeDescription: Caucasus mountains, from far southwestern russia eastward to northeastern azerbaijan and southward to northeastern turkey, armenia, and far northwestern iran
description: Large gamebird endemic to the mountains of the Caucasus region. Male is jet-black with a tiny white patch on the shoulder, a tail that curves downwards at the tip, and flaming red “eyebrows.” White underwing patches are displayed during jumping lekking display.

name: Bush Blackcap
rangeDescription: Eastern south africa (southward to central eastern cape) and western eswatini
description: A large warbler that is remarkably bulbul-like, pale gray-buff below and olive-brown above with an orange-pink bill and a black cap that extends below the eye. The juvenile is duller.

name: Victorin's Warbler
rangeDescription: Southwestern south africa (western cape and southern eastern cape)
description: A skulky brownish warbler with a ragged tail, warm cinnamon-buff underparts, and a distinctive gray face with a pale yellow eye. It is restricted to damp fynbos, especially boggy areas with sedges and Berzelia, and fern-filled glades along forest edges, where it creeps about mouse-like and is almost always first detected by its characteristic song.

name: Grant's Bluebill
rangeDescription: Primary forest of eastern democratic republic of the congo and southwestern uganda
description: A large, chunky-headed black-and-red forest waxbill with a blue-and-red bill. Sexes differ: the male has a red forehead extending to the midcrown and eyes that appear to be rimmed by black spectacles, while the female has white spots on the belly and red only on the throat and rump.

name: White-headed Marsh Tyrant
rangeDescription: Colombia to trinidad, the guianas, southern brazil, and northern argentina
description: Small flycatcher always found near water such as lakes, ponds, and marshes where it perches conspicuously. Males are quite unique in being black with a white head, while females are grayish-brown above and pale below with a white forehead and throat.

name: Spectacled Duck
rangeDescription: Mainly forested regions of southern argentina and chile
description: A handsome, generally uncommon, and rather shy duck of quiet vegetated lakes, forested rivers, and marshy wetlands; no similar species in range. Usually found in pairs or family groups, sometimes associating with other ducks but as often slightly separate.

name: Dot-eared Coquette
rangeDescription: Lowlands of north-central brazil to eastern bolivia (santa cruz)
description: Tiny charismatic hummingbird. Note the male’s white cheeks tufts with green spots.

name: Carunculated Caracara
rangeDescription: Páramo of southwestern colombia and ecuador
description: Strikingly patterned raptor of the high Andes in Ecuador and southern Colombia. Note pied plumage pattern, white streaks on black breast, and orange face.
